page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory. The hardware configuration includes 446 GB of local SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The CPU architecture is x86_64, utilizing 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core, and includes support for AVX, AVX512F, AES, and FMA instruction sets.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates modest compute capabilities. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, position the processor in the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, memory read bandwidth and Passmark database operations fall into the lower performance brackets. However, the instance maintains average performance in large-block memory write bandwidth and Passmark CPU extended instruction tests. LLM inference speeds for small 135M models are average, though performance drops significantly to the bottom 10% when handling larger 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i1.2xlarge offers a balanced resource profile with dedicated CPU allocation and bundled local SSD storage. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring dedicated physical cores and local storage without needing high-performance compute or memory bandwidth. The primary tradeoff is the older Intel Xeon architecture, which limits its suitability for modern, CPU-intensive tasks.

This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, lightweight database operations, and development environments that benefit from dedicated CPU cores and local SSD storage but do not demand high-throughput processing.
